channel.title: The art of Kyle Parker Cunningham - hand-colored
channel.description: Artist portfolio featuring painting, printmaking, and cinema

item.title: Bottled Oxygen
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Two bell jars share a hose: in one, a small yellow-leafed tree; in the other, a village of little dome houses, with a tap to meter the air between them. The tree works, the houses breathe. The future's utilities may be exactly this intimate.

item.title: Elephant Mask
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Behind the bright yellow elephant mask: an elephant. "We all wear masks most of the time," the painting said back in 2018 — and the most convincing disguise is always yourself, slightly off.

item.title: Gardener
item.author: Unknown
item.description: The whale tows a coracle planted with a tree — the print of Tugboat (Whale & Sequoia). The gardener of the future sea, mid-row, unhurried. Whales transplanting trees: I keep saying it because they keep doing it.

item.title: In The Pines
item.author: Unknown
item.description: Six pines, hand colored in six different greens, standing in their own quiet. Named for the place where shadows stack vertical and the needles make their own floor — and maybe a little for the old song.

item.title: Tubed Pachyderm
item.author: Unknown
item.description: An elephant refitted as a tube amplifier — vacuum tubes standing on its back, speaker cones set into its flank, a field of red gouache behind. The herd's volume restored by analog means. (I have opinions about analog; see the Olympus typewriter.)

item.title: Abduction
item.author: Unknown

item.title: Blue Corn
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A tall figure stands very still on the orange ground, balancing an ear of blue corn on its head — and on the corn, an origami crane, also standing very still. Patience, practiced as agriculture. Corn is the oldest engineering project in this valley; see also the painting Three Blue Corn.

Based on two earlier 2016 oil paintings of the same title (neither yet documented here).

item.title: Ghost Thugs
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
There will always be individuals being individuals.

Seven small ghosts in a lineup at the bottom of a scratched sky — and one of them, gold, clearly refusing the dress code.

item.title: Nogal Canyon
item.author: Unknown
item.description: I scratched this plate sitting in an arroyo in Nogal Canyon while on a camping trip with friends. This was near the windmill if you ever wanted to find the exact spot it would be down canyon from the windmill in the arroyo.

item.title: Olympus
item.author: Unknown
item.description: This is one of my favorite typewriters of all time. Unfortunately it has a sticky "n" key, it works, but you get some type errors. That, though, is the cost of being analog!

item.title: Rocket Propelled Clovis Point
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A turtle carries the arsenal this time — rocket, clovis point, and satellite dish strapped to the hexagons of its shell. The slowest courier entrusted with the fastest cargo: twelve thousand years of point technology riding deep time's own armored chassis. The painting (2020) posed the idea; the turtle volunteered to deliver it.

Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. Handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

item.title: Skull
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A skull in profile, hand colored a pale mineral green — the oldest still life subject there is. More curiosity than warning: this is the architecture under every portrait I've ever painted.

Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. Handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

Based on an earlier 2015 oil painting of the same title (not yet documented here).

item.title: Submerged
item.author: Unknown
item.description: A diver stands on the bottom, helmet line wandering all the way up to the thin band of the surface. Sibling of Deep Sea (2018) — the same predicament, revisited.

item.title: Sunflowers
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Sunflowers in a mug, the big head spiraling with seed, hand colored in burnt orange. Numbered into the plate one pull at a time — an open-ended series, with each numbered print getting its portrait below.

Intaglio Drypoint Print.

Versions

Each print is printed in an open ended series. I physically scratch the print number into the plate before inking it and then print just one copy at that number.

Below are the various prints I've made of this plate:

item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A figure stands easy on green ground in a gold space helmet, oxygen tank resting at the knee. A vacation in the future may require equipment, but the posture is eternal: shoulders down, nowhere to be, air supply secured.

intaglio drypoint prints printed area approx 6 x 9 inches handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches

item.title: stole the rainbow
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Everyone is trying to find what is at the end of the rainbow. Some of us just have more effective tactics than others.

8 x 10 inches drypoint intaglio print hand painted with watercolor and gouache

item.title: balance
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
drypoint intaglio printmaking on rives bfk, handcolored with gouache 8 by 10 inches 2021

Finding balance in the forest. Everything is something and is something else at the same time. All is connected and coincidence rules the day. Tomorrow I find myself ideal in balance and rhythm with the trees.

item.title: airlift
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Future cranes crafted from recycled libraries. They soar up on thermals. Voice heard echoing canyons. The float towards the sun. Find clouds along the way. Absconding back to the moon.

Intaglio Drypoint Print Image Size: 6 x 9 inches Paper Size roughly 8 x 10 inches

Based on an earlier 2015 oil painting of the same title (not yet documented here).

Drypoint Intaglio Print 8 inches by 10 inches July 18th, 2021

item.title: rocks glass
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
This particular glass was my grandfathers. He drank from it nightly a 7-up and vodka.

8 x 10 inches drypoint intaglio print hand painted with watercolor and gouache

item.title: Six
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Six round creatures on bird feet, eyes up on long stalks, hand colored in purples and blues, standing around the way a group does when nobody wants to leave first. Cousin to the Seven painting; apparently I count my crowds.

Drypoint Intaglio Print, 8 x 10 inches. Handcolored with watercolor.

item.title: Pruning
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Loppers at work on a prickly pear, a green barrel cactus standing witness. Garden chores in the desert are a negotiation between species, and the cactus usually gets the last word. Hand colored.

Intaglio drypoint prints. Printed area approx 6 x 9 inches, handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

item.title: Lunarem
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Twenty-eight moons in their phases, row by row, drawn from the years I spent painting the Earth's oldest timepiece (Cyclum Lunarem, 2014–2018). The moon repeats itself and is never the same twice — which is also a fair description of pulling prints from one plate.

8 x 10 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Handcolored with watercolor. 2018.

item.title: Teardrop
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
The teardrop trailer — the Homemade Spaceship. Jeannie and I built one and lived in it for a year crossing the American West, so this is less a still life than a portrait of a home. Red and white, hand colored, permanently ready to leave.

8 x 10 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Handcolored with watercolor. 2018.

item.title: Kite
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
An elephant with her kite.

Sometimes life is stranger than fiction.

Pretending us humans with our myriad distractions would be the first to ever notice extra terrestrials is the kind of anthropocentric folly we are all to easily fooled by.

If aliens did magically appear is almost certain the world of animals and plants will be the first to notice. They live in and of the natural world not on top of it. Ever observant, life for them depends upon knowing exactly what is happening around them at all times. If something was amiss in our atmosphere and outer space creeps were lurking in the shadows I'll put my faith into spiders and elk knowing before anyone else.

Elephants have generational knowledge carefully curated and shared since time immortal. I'm pretty sure if they find a little flying saucer poking around the Savannah they will probably already know with it is and what to do with it.

I imagine they will fly it as a kite, because what could be more fun for a trunk than a kite.

8 by 10 inches. Drypoint intaglio print. Watercolor added by hand. 2018.

item.title: 120 Volts
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A long, stooped figure plugged into the wall outlet by his own hair. Household current as life support, five years before the sky demonstrated the high-voltage version on me personally. The glitch of daily reality at its most literal: we are all on the grid.

intaglio printmaking on rives bfk. 8 by 10 inches. 2018.

item.title: Stole the Rainbow
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Someone has cut the middle out of the rainbow and is walking off with it across the clouds, leaving the two ends standing there like an unfinished bridge. Hand colored, naturally — it's the only print where the color is the loot. Pulled again in 2021.

5 x 5 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Handcolored with watercolor. 2018.

item.title: Deep Sea
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A figure in a diving helmet stands on the bottom, while a single line wanders all the way up to the thin green-and-red band of the surface, impossibly far above. Some days are like that. The air is up there somewhere.

8 x 10 inches. Drypoint Intaglio Print. Handcolored with watercolor. 2018.

item.title: Tecate
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
A Tecate can, slightly crushed, hand colored red. The desert has its monuments and its sacraments; this one is both. Still life raises the authority of simple, mundane objects — sometimes the object is a cold beer at the end of a hot day.

intaglio drypoint prints. printed area approx 6 x 9 inches. handtorn paper approx 8 x 10 inches.

item.title: Field Theory AP
item.author: Unknown
item.description:
Concentric rectangles closing in on a small blue center — the field drawn as pure attention. The same image became a mural in Truth or Consequences; this is the pocket version. Artist proof.

8 x 10 inches. drypoint intaglio print. hand painted with watercolor and gauche. 2018.
